rv.q: Here physicality is paired with a contemporary, empathic wit and sensitivity, which stops a potentially mawkish story from ever becoming too saccharine.
It runs out of steam at the end, with a slightly woo-woo finale that feels needlessly silly, bordering on actual cringe.
Whilst the narrative may conform and play out with a certain predictability, the journey is everything and here, it proves a captivating and utterly wonderful experience.
A hugely relatable and perceptive show with generous doses of physicality.
The writing isn’t as reliable nor as poetic as it believes it is, but the direction makes up for it.
Frantic Assembly’s Lost Atoms, written by Anna Jordan and directed by Scott Graham, is a tender and quietly devastating exploration of how we love and how we remember.
This is an impressive, visually compelling production fronted by a duo with undeniable chemistry, and it encompasses all that Frantic Assembly does best in the form of a fresh, engaging story.
Lost Atoms shows that the company have as much to offer the theatre 30 years on as they did as a fledgling student group.
Frantic Assembly's love play is incomplete and inaudible.
Sad to say, it’s not so much atoms that are lost as an entire evening.
It’s a tender and moving play well worth seeing.

cn.t: Frantic Assembly's signature physicality elevates a conventional love story, with critics praising the tender performances and inventive staging, though some find the underlying script too familiar to fully resonate.
